body:
Part of #665 (Mark II split). Owner request 2026-11-10: bring up the split image on the Arty A7-100T, beside the AX7101's release bench. Depends on S9 (#870), whose builder recipe makes split images. Relates to #583 (Arty configurations) and #829 (gPTP on MII).

**Scope.**
- One Arty configuration with `control.placement: split` at the 1x1 shape, through S9's recipe. 100 Mb/s MII carries 1x1, not 8x8.
- DDR3 is left out, as on every split image (decision D4). The system clock is set without DDR3's 83.333 MHz window, and the choice is stated.
- The build-time latency pair keeps the board's calibration; any bench compensation is written at runtime only and never tracked.
- A defect found on the board is fixed here only if it is small and has a regression test that fails without it; otherwise it gets its own issue.

**Acceptance.**
1. **Build.**
   - S9's identity gate passes on the Arty manifest.
   - The split simulation boots to ready.
   - Routed WNS and WHS are at or above 0 at every corner, recorded against the +0.030 ns floor. A bench image, not a release image.
   - LUT, FF and BRAM are reported.
2. **Boot.**
   - The firmware reaches ready on the UART.
   - The ident string names the split placement, and the mailbox `ID` register reads the contract version.
3. **Link and enumeration.**
   - Link at 100 Mb/s.
   - The controller enumerates the entity.
   - Every descriptor is byte-identical to the all-fabric Arty image's, or each difference is explained against IEEE 1722.1-2021 and Milan v1.2.
4. **gPTP.**
   - asCapable and sync to the bench grandmaster (IEEE 802.1AS-2020 10.2, 11.2), with offset and peer delay recorded over at least 10 minutes.
   - Any runtime compensation is stated beside each figure.
5. **Streams** (Milan v1.2 5.5; IEEE 802.1Q-2022 35).
   - One talker and one listener connection with the reference peer.
   - Every stream counter is read.
   - Frames are checked on the capture.
6. **Soak.** One hour with both connections up, every counter recorded before and after, and no discontinuity.
7. **Save.** One descriptor change saved and read back after a reset, with the save time measured. The measurement feeds #876's model (save time proportional to the data saved). The Arty's flash differs from the AX7101's, so the figure is the Arty's own.

**Out of scope.**
- 8x8.
- Power cycles: the Arty has no remote power control.
- S12 (the AX7101 split bench) and the flip (S13).

comments.body:
[A764] TAKEN
Branch: `878-arty-bringup`, at S9's head `ad2ed0e3` (`665-s9-split-image`, which has not moved). PR to `dev-soft-core`, stacked on S9's.
Authoritative references: #878 (scope, acceptance 1 to 7); #870 (S9: the split recipe `--placement split`, the image manifest, `check_image_identity.py`, the split boot simulation); #665 plan stages S9 and S12, decisions D2 and D7, #640 D4 (no DDR3 in a split image), the owner's 2026-10-30 decision on the split CPU clock; #583 (Arty configurations); #829 (gPTP on MII and the board's latency calibration); IEEE 1722.1-2021, Milan v1.2 5.5, IEEE 802.1AS-2020 10.2 and 11.2, IEEE 802.1Q-2022 35.
Interpreted scope: one Arty configuration at the shape of `endstation_arty_current` (one AAF listener with CRF, one AAF talker), built at `control.placement: split` through S9's recipe, with no DDR3, a system clock chosen from the board's 100 MHz oscillator with the reason stated, and the board's calibrated gPTP latency pair as its build-time values; the builder and documentation entries it needs, regenerated by their generators; every AX7101 export byte-identical. On the Arty, in order: boot to ready with the split ident and the mailbox `ID`; link at 100 Mb/s; enumeration, every descriptor compared byte for byte with the all-fabric Arty image's and each difference explained by clause or called a defect; gPTP; one connection each way with the reference peer; a one-hour soak; one saved descriptor change read back after a reset, its save time against the bytes written as one point of #876's model.
Validation plan: the identity gate on the built image; the split boot simulation at the Arty shape; the route's WNS and WHS at every corner against the +0.030 ns floor, with LUT, FF and BRAM; the builder suite and the AX7101 byte-identical exports; `docs_inventory.py --check` and `check_doc_style.py`; every hosted job step of `dev-soft-core`'s workflows on a clean clone of the final head; `git diff --check` against the merge base; bench receipts per acceptance item.
Blockers: two, which items 4 to 6 depend on:
- `dev-soft-core` does not carry PR #831 (merged on `dev` on 2026-11-02), the MII launch fix for #829. Its merge base with `dev` is `1f29f189`. Without that fix the fabric gPTP plane times no frame on the MII port (#829's first fault), so asCapable cannot rise on this board.
- The runtime write of the latency pair, which the tap compensation needs, was never merged on `dev` or `dev-soft-core`; it exists only in #829's bench evidence. Without it no compensation can be written at runtime.
Items 1 to 3 and 7 go first. Items 4 to 6 are measured as far as this tree allows, and recorded.

[A764] STOP

Head: `cfcd863edfaed84b8f2ff135261985653bb5b0ab` on `878-arty-bringup` (local, not pushed). It is three commits on S9's `ad2ed0e3`, which has not moved. Configuration, generated include, builder test and documentation only: no HDL, firmware, mailbox contract, builder code or VERSION change.

**Why STOP: items 2 to 7 cannot be met in this lane. Each of the three causes lies outside it.**

1. **The split image cannot boot on hardware: #791.**
   - The CPU generator decodes the 224 KiB control ROM as `(addr & 0xfffc8000) == 0`, so every fetch at or above 0x8000 faults and the core restarts without a word.
   - On the board the image configures (DONE 1, no CRC error, normal configuration from flash), and its UART stays silent: 90 s after the write, after two console resets, and after a second write.
   - The image's own CPU netlist carries that mask three times.
   - The firmware's second call in `main`, `nvm_flash_litespi_power_on`, is at 0x11c00, before the console exists.
   - A scratch image changed only in the region list it hands the CPU generator (the power-of-two cover the boot harness uses) runs the same firmware. It prints `boot` and then `ready` 32 ms later.
   - That fix changes every split image's CPU netlist, the AX7101's included, which this lane must leave unchanged. #791 also carries its own design choice, CPU-simulation test and mutant.
2. **The bench needs its owner.**
   - The controller does not answer on the network. It has not answered since the bench machines restarted around 18:00.
   - The tap's capture interfaces have link but have received 0 frames since the capture host booted.
   - So enumeration, both connections, the soak, the save through ATDECC and every frame check cannot run.
3. **gPTP on MII needs #831.** It merged on `dev` on 2026-11-02, after `dev-soft-core`'s merge base `1f29f189`.
   - On the scratch image above, the plane shows #829's first fault: itself as grandmaster, peer delay 0, asCapable 0, at 12 of 12 polls over 120 s.
   - The all-fabric image the board carried before reads `SYNC=1 ASCAPABLE=1 PDELAY_NS=2` on the same link with the true 1409/100 pair. The tap appears to be bypassed, so no compensation would be needed now.
   - The runtime latency pair was never merged in any case.

**S9's branch moved during this lane**, to `1e1fd9ef`: a `KL_mbx` round that registers the host read data and the receive ring write, S9's option (a). It had not moved when this lane started, so it is not merged here.
- This branch stays stacked on `ad2ed0e3`.
- Its route figures are `ad2ed0e3`'s `KL_mbx`. A rebuild on S9's new head would also re-measure the 100 MHz option.
- That round does not touch #791.

**Decisions or actions needed:**
- (a) #791 fixed in its own lane, then this image rebuilt.
- (b) The controller and the tap capture brought back by the owner.
- (c) The `dev` -> `dev-soft-core` sync carrying #831.

**Item 1, met:**
- **The configuration.** `configs/endstation_arty_split.yaml` has `endstation_arty_current`'s shape and is built at `control.placement: split` through S9's recipe. It differs in three keys:
  - the system clock, 80 MHz;
  - `srp.rtl_table`, false;
  - the board's 1409/100 latency pair from #829.
  - It states no `control:` key, because the publication census reads every `configs/*.yaml` as an all-fabric shape and refuses a file that states `split`.
- **The clock, 80 MHz.**
  - A split image builds no DDR3 (#640 D4).
  - 100 MHz misses on this -1 part: slow-corner WNS -0.822 ns, 3,529 failing endpoints, all in `KL_mbx` on the bus clock (S9's open item).
  - 80 MHz divides exactly from the 100 MHz oscillator beside the PHY, datapath and IDELAY clocks, and the latency pair was measured at it.
  - In this tree the split CPU runs on the 50 MHz datapath clock, not on `sys`, so 80 MHz moves only the bus, the mailbox, the UART and the flash.
- **The identity gate passes** on the built image: ident `... baremetal split`, mailbox 2.4, firmware sha256 `5fcdfa5b...`, bitstream payload `656730ce...` bound in the manifest.
- **The split simulation boots to ready** at the Arty shape in 75.032 ms (6,002,576 bus cycles at 80 MHz), trace 18 of 18 equal.
- **Routed at every corner:**
  - Slow: WNS +0.140 ns, WHS +0.102 ns.
  - Fast: WNS +1.634 ns, WHS +0.019 ns.
  - The +0.030 ns floor is met, and all 64,054 nets are routed.
- **Utilization:** 30,811 LUT (48.60 %), 36,750 FF, 64.5 block RAM tiles (50 RAMB36 and 29 RAMB18), 5 DSP.
- **The AX7101 images are unchanged.** The builder's outputs of every shipped config, all-fabric and at `--placement split`, are byte-identical to `ad2ed0e3`'s: 100 files, 40 of them the AX7101's.
- **The flashed image is this head's.** A clean clone of `ff43755f` reproduces its ELF, CSR map, flash layout, manifest, ROM bank images and constraints. The two later commits touch only the build guide and the builder test.
- **The model id is kept.** The generated AEM image is byte-identical to the all-fabric Arty's (5,952 B, CRC `574d3f5d`), so IEEE 1722.1-2021 6.2.2.8 asks for no new one.

**Gates, all rc 0, each on its own clean clone (of `cfcd863e` unless stated):**
- **The hosted jobs this change touches, every `run:` step:**
  - docs: docs-gates-0, docs-gates-1, docs-gates-2 and docs-check, 84 steps;
  - elaborate: both builder legs with elaboration and the aggregator, 41 steps;
  - rtl-fast: changes and firmware-unit, 14 steps;
  - reused from `519bab1f`, because between the two heads only `sw/builder/test_builder.py` changed and these jobs do not read it: wire-accountability, docs-check-no-git, publication-census (7 shapes and its self-test) and behave, 24 steps.
- The builder legs read `ALL GATES PASS EXCEPT 1 NOT RUN`: gate 1b's `MAKEFLAGS` mutation, which this host's make cannot run, and gate 11's calibration report, which is not on disk.
- The first pass at `519bab1f` failed builder leg 1. Gate 36a held a per-config rate table without the new config. `cfcd863e` adds the config with its true 48, 96 and 192 kHz.
- The split boot simulation at `cfcd863e`.
- The identity gate on the built image.
- The builder export compare, `ad2ed0e3` against `519bab1f`; no builder code or configuration changed after it.
- `git diff --check` against `ad2ed0e3` and against `1d6bf555`.
- **Not run:** `rtl.yml` (the full sweep's shard jobs, `yosys-shards`, `yosys-portability` and `physical-gptp`); in `rtl-fast.yml`, `verilator-lint`, `yosys-tool`, `yosys-elaboration`, `split-cdc`, `firmware-boundary`, `firmware-verilator` and the three mutant shards; and the API jobs. This change has no HDL, firmware or harness change, and the lane stops here. `docs_inventory --check` does not exist at this head.

**Bench as left:**
- The Arty carries this head's image, silent (#791). A reset restores the same silent boot.
- `-hupcl` is set on the console port. Restoring it at 23:01 reset the board once, as expected.
- The bench lock is free, and nothing of mine remains on another host.

[A10] **Ruling on [A764]'s STOP at `cfcd863e`.** Item 1 is accepted as met. Items 2 to 7 wait for the three causes the STOP names.

1. **#791, the region decode:** its own lane opens now on `dev-soft-core`. The preferred fix is (a), power-of-two sub-regions in the region list, as the scratch image on the board proved. Once it merges, this branch takes it and the image is rebuilt.
2. **#831 on `dev-soft-core`:** a `dev` -> `dev-soft-core` sync runs after the two split PRs now at merge (S7 and #823). This branch then takes that sync.
3. **Bench:** the controller and the capture host are down. Bringing them back is the owner's job, and this lane does not touch them.
4. **Clock, 80 MHz:** accepted for this board at 1x1. 100 MHz misses in `KL_mbx`, which is S9's open round. Re-measure 100 MHz on S9's final head when this lane resumes, and keep 80 MHz unless 100 MHz meets the floor. At 1x1 the CPU load then scales by 100/80 from S2b's figure at 100 MHz; state it beside the load.
5. **Resume:** one round, after (1) and (2) land and the bench is back. It merges S9's final head, #791 and the sync, rebuilds, and runs items 2 to 7 in order. Until then nothing in this lane runs.

[A10] **#878 resumes now (round 2). It no longer waits for the merges.** The bench is back: the controller and the capture host are up, and the bench lock is free.

1. **Branch inputs.** Merge, each as its own merge commit and in this order:
   - S9's head `a91fb27d` (PR #889: timing met at every corner; its round 4 is tests and docs only);
   - #791's head `03447eaa` (PR #888: the exact region decode; its round 2 is docs and a guard);
   - #831's merge on `dev`, `e61a4afa` (gPTP on MII).

   Only `docs/design/MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md` and `docs/reference/FR_NFR.md` conflict. Keep both sides' facts. Any other conflict is a STOP with its paths.
2. **Clock.** Re-measure 100 MHz on this tree, as the ruling of issuecomment-6788749916 item 4 says. Keep 80 MHz unless 100 MHz meets the +0.030 ns floor at every corner on the best of the three #818 directives. At 1x1, state the CPU load scaled to the chosen clock beside S2b's 0.450.
3. **Image.** Rebuild through S9's recipe, then run the identity gate and the split simulation's boot to ready. Show that the AX7101 exports are byte-identical to the merged inputs' own.
4. **Bench:** items 2 to 7 of #878 in order, as round 1's prompt sets them, under the bench rules. A failed check after a sound build is a result. Find its root cause and fix it here only if the fix is small and comes with a test; otherwise record it for its own issue and continue.
5. **The PR** comes after the official `dev` -> `dev-soft-core` sync and #791 have merged. The manager then moves this branch onto them; the bench evidence carries over when the image inputs are unchanged.

[A764b] TAKEN
Branch: `878-arty-bringup`, at round 1's head `cfcd863e`. PR to `dev-soft-core`, stacked on S9's; the manager opens it after the `dev` -> `dev-soft-core` sync and #791 merge.
Authoritative references: #878 (acceptance 1 to 7) and the round 2 ruling (issuecomment-6798352202); the clock ruling (issuecomment-6788749916, item 4); #870 (S9: the split recipe, the image manifest, the identity gate, the split boot simulation); #665 plan stages S9 and S12, decisions D2, D4 and D7; #791 (the exact region decode); #831 (gPTP on MII); #818 (the three placement directives and the floor); #583 (Arty configurations); #829 (the board's latency calibration and the tap compensation); #876 (the save-time model); IEEE 1722.1-2021, Milan v1.2 5.5, IEEE 802.1AS-2020 10.2 and 11.2, IEEE 802.1Q-2022 35.
Interpreted scope: merge, each as its own merge commit and in this order, S9's head `a91fb27d`, #791's head `03447eaa` and #831's merge `e61a4afa`, keeping both sides' facts in the two documents the ruling names; any other conflict stops the lane. Re-measure the Arty split at 100 MHz on the three #818 placement directives from one synthesis checkpoint, and keep 80 MHz unless the best of them meets the +0.030 ns floor at every corner; state the 1x1 CPU load scaled to the chosen clock beside S2b's 0.450. Rebuild the image through S9's recipe and run the identity gate and the split boot simulation; show every AX7101 export byte-identical to the merged inputs' own. Then, on the board, items 2 to 7 in order: boot to ready with the split ident and the mailbox `ID`; link at 100 Mb/s, enumeration and every descriptor compared byte for byte with the all-fabric Arty image's; gPTP over at least 10 minutes with the runtime tap compensation computed from a fresh zero and stated beside every figure; one connection each way with the reference peer, every stream counter read, frames on the capture; a one-hour soak; one saved descriptor change read back after a reset, its save time against the bytes written as one point of #876's model. A defect found on the board is fixed here only if it is small and comes with a test that fails without it; otherwise it is recorded for its own issue.
Validation plan: the route's WNS and WHS at every corner and directive against the floor, with LUT, FF and BRAM; the identity gate on the built image; the split boot simulation at the Arty shape; the builder suite and the byte-identical AX7101 exports; `docs_inventory.py --check` and `check_doc_style.py`; every hosted job step of `dev-soft-core`'s workflows on a clean clone of the final head; `git diff --check` against the merge base; bench receipts per acceptance item.
Blockers: none known at start.

[A764b] STOP

Head: `a80ed3d5cd5055a1d768a89fecdd4563047c6709` on `878-arty-bringup` (local, not pushed). It is round 1's `cfcd863e` plus the first ruled merge, S9's head `a91fb27d`, which merged with no conflict.

**Why STOP: the second ruled merge, #791's head `03447eaa`, conflicts in `sw/litex/test_ctrl_memory.py`.** The ruling names only `docs/design/MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md` and `docs/reference/FR_NFR.md` as expected conflicts and makes any other conflict a STOP. That merge is aborted, and the branch stays at the S9 merge.

**The conflict** is one line of the module docstring, which lists what the suite grades.
- S9's `0f3c4756` adds item 8, the out-of-context mapper's arms. That commit has been on this branch since round 1 (from `ad2ed0e3`), so the conflict comes up whatever the merge order.
- #791's `eb26f22d` adds a different item 8, the CPU decode arm.
- Both sides change the header from "seven things" to "eight things" in the same way.
- The code merges with no textual conflict: #791's import, its `decode.arms` in `main()` and in the mutant table, its `cpu_regions` result field, and S9's mapper arm all come through.

**Proposed resolution, which keeps both sides' facts:** item 8 is the out-of-context mapper and item 9 is the CPU decode, and the header reads "nine things". I have not run the suite on it, because no CPUs were free to book.

**The third merge, #831's `e61a4afa`,** was trial-merged on a scratch clone after that resolution. It conflicts only in the two documents the ruling names.

**Decision needed:** accept this resolution for `sw/litex/test_ctrl_memory.py`, or name another. This lane then resumes at the #791 merge.

**Nothing else has run in round 2:** no route, image or simulation, and no bench action. The bench lock was not taken. The Arty still carries round 1's image, which is silent because of #791.

[A10] **Ruling on [A764b]'s STOP:** the proposed resolution is accepted. In `sw/litex/test_ctrl_memory.py`'s docstring, item 8 is the mapper, item 9 is the CPU decode, and the header says "nine things". Complete the #791 merge with it, then the #831 merge. Any further conflict that touches only docstrings, comments or documentation lists is resolved by keeping both sides' facts, with no STOP; any conflict in code or tests is still a STOP. Merge S9's ruled head `a91fb27d`, not `a69fc0f5`: its round 4 is tests and docs only, and the manager moves the branch later. Book CPUs as they free up.

[A764b] STOP

Head: `7f9a7febc2f4b9a2feafe35d74934bca9bdee822` on `878-arty-bringup` (local, not pushed). It holds round 1's three commits, the three ruled merges and two new commits:
- the merges: S9's `a91fb27d` as `a80ed3d5`; #791's `03447eaa` as `895d98a4`, with the ruled docstring resolution; #831's `e61a4afa` as `890e7287`, keeping both sides' facts in `FR_NFR.md` and `MARK_II_AREA_PLAN.md`;
- `6c01e5e1`: the configuration's system clock is now 100 MHz;
- `7f9a7feb`: the build guide.

**Why STOP: items 3, 5, 6 and 7, and item 4's offset, need the bench's controller and capture. Neither can serve the bench, and both need the owner.**
- The controller host answers, but its bench interface has no carrier. I checked six times between 15:49 and 18:12. Its ADP discovery finds no entity.
- The capture host answers, but both tap interfaces have received 0 frames since it booted. The Arty's peer delay reads 2 to 13 ns on the true pair. So the tap is not in the Arty's link either: under the tap, #829 read about 888 ns on the same pair.
- If the tap goes back in, asCapable needs a runtime compensation, and this tree cannot write one. `0x540` and `0x544` are inert here, because #829's writable pair was never in a PR.

**Item 1 is met, at 100 MHz.** At this tree's `KL_mbx`, the -1 part meets #818's floor (+0.030 ns setup, 0 ns hold) at every corner, at each of the three placement directives, from one synthesis checkpoint.

| sys | Placement directive | Slow WNS / WHS, ns | Fast WNS / WHS, ns | LUT | FF | BRAM tiles |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 100 MHz | `ExtraTimingOpt`, the board's flow, the flashed image | +0.378 / +0.105 | +1.638 / +0.007 | 30,491 (48.09 %) | 36,925 | 64.5 (50 RAMB36, 29 RAMB18) |
| 100 MHz | `ExtraPostPlacementOpt` | +0.203 / +0.156 | +1.683 / +0.018 | 30,480 | 36,925 | 64.5 |
| 100 MHz | `AltSpreadLogic_high` | +0.156 / +0.105 | +1.638 / +0.007 | 30,491 | 36,925 | 64.5 |
| 80 MHz | `ExtraTimingOpt`, not chosen | +0.071 / +0.104 | +1.634 / +0.013 | 30,311 | 36,917 | 64.5 |

- Every run has 0 failing endpoints and every net routed, and the image uses 5 DSP.
- The worst setup path at 100 MHz is `KL_mbx/u_tx/ch_r` to `u_tx/widx_r`'s enable (12 levels). WHS is below +0.030 ns at both clocks, on a 50 MHz datapath path into the CSR snapshot.
- The latency pair was measured at an 80 MHz system clock, and two of its ingress terms cross into it. The configuration keeps the pair.
- **CPU load at 1x1:** S2b's 0.450 is at a 100 MHz CPU clock, so at 100 MHz the factor is 1.00 and the load stays 0.450. In this tree the split CPU still runs on the 50 MHz datapath clock (`milan_soc.py:3586`), because S2b's clock move is not merged. There the same scaling gives 0.900, over the 0.70 ceiling. That figure is a scaling, not a measurement.
- **The identity gate passes** on the built image: placement split, ident `... baremetal split`, mailbox 2.4, and the bitstream payload bound in the manifest.
- **The split boot simulation boots to ready** at the Arty shape in 73.165 ms, with 0 findings.
- **#791's region-decode test passes** at the Arty shape, with 0 findings. The CPU netlist carries the exact masks and no `fffc8000`.
- **The firmware is the same bytes as round 1's 100 MHz build.** The AEM image is byte-identical to the all-fabric Arty's (5,952 B), so no new model id is needed.
- **A clean clone of the head reproduces the flashed image's inputs.** They are equal apart from time stamps and the order of the top Verilog's hierarchy comment tree.
- **The AX7101 images are unchanged.** A scratch merge of the three inputs without this lane's commits differs from the head's merges by exactly round 1's three commits. The builder's outputs of every shipped configuration, all-fabric and split, are byte-identical between that merge and both `890e7287` and the head: 100 files, 40 of them the AX7101's.

**Item 2: the image boots to ready on the board.** After the flash (rcs 0/0/0, verified by read-back), the console printed `boot` and then `ready` 16 ms later.
- **Mailbox `ID`, shown in part:** `ready` follows `mbx_open()`, which refuses unless `ID`'s magic and major equal the contract and its capabilities match.
- **The minor and the ident are shown at image level only:** by the identity gate and the flash's read-back. The split console prints neither.

**Item 4: asCapable and sync to the bench grandmaster, met.**
- `SYNC=1 ASCAPABLE=1` at 66 of 66 polls over 10 min 50 s (IEEE 802.1AS-2020 10.2, 11.2).
- The grandmaster and parent are the bench's, with path count 2.
- Peer delay: mean 6.7 ns, sd 3.0, range 2 to 13 ns.
- **No runtime compensation:** the true 1409/100 pair was applied at every poll.
- **The offset is not recorded.** The capture receives no frame, and the console has no offset field.
- **Link at 100 Mb/s is inferred, not read.** No PHY status is readable on the split console.

**Gates on a clean clone of the head.** Each job was replayed natively, every `run:` step as hosted.
- **23 jobs replayed:** the docs workflow (6), elaborate (3) and rtl-fast (14).
  - Every rtl-fast and elaborate job succeeded. The elaborate legs read `ALL GATES PASS EXCEPT 1 NOT RUN`: gate 11's calibration report, which is not on this host's disk.
  - Of the docs jobs, docs-gates-1, docs-gates-2, wire-accountability and docs-check-no-git succeeded.
- **One failure, from the merge combination, not from this lane's commits:** docs-gates-0's Python idiom gate reads `FAIL: long module 11 > ratchet 10`, and the docs-check aggregator fails with it.
  - `sw/litex/test_ctrl_memory.py` has 996 lines at S9's head and 1000 at #791's, against the 1000-line limit.
  - Merged, it has 1003.
  - The same file cut to 1000 lines passes the gate.
  - The fix belongs to whichever of #888 and #889 lands second on `dev-soft-core`. Raising the ratchet would weaken the gate.
- docs-gates-0's ten later steps, which the job skipped after that gate, were run by hand on the same head: all rc 0.
- Also run: the split boot simulation, the region-decode test, the export compare, and `git diff --check` against the merge base `1d6bf555` and against `cfcd863e`, all rc 0.
- **Not run:** `rtl.yml`, which runs once a PR is marked ready, and the API jobs. `docs_inventory --check` does not exist at this head.

**Decisions or actions needed:**
- (a) The owner restores the controller's bench link and the tap capture. If the tap is out by design, say so, and item 4 needs no compensation.
- (b) The 3-line cut of `test_ctrl_memory.py`, in #888 or #889, or here if ruled.

**Bench as left:**
- The Arty runs this head's 100 MHz image, at asCapable and sync on the true pair. A reset restores the same image and pair; no runtime write was made.
- `-hupcl` is set on the console port. Clearing it at 15:49 reset the board once, as expected.
- The bench lock is free.
